analysis.title: GS MORNING: 1) Connecting you to GS, 2) Data Centre Forecasts, 3) NZD Update, 4) Latest FX Trader and 5) Week Ahead Previews
key_insights: After the US midterms, data centre stocks fell first while the rest of the market rose. The next day the rest of the market caught down to the data centre trade. GS Trading's Privorotsky says semis down 10% creates leveraged supply, triggers Nasdaq levels and puts the market in a short gamma environment.

Alec Phillips expects federal focus on data centres to be limited to ratepayer protections and possibly removing some tax incentives. At the state level the issue is permitting moratoria, with gubernatorial wins in Texas, Georgia and Ohio putting up to about 40% of planned capacity in theory at risk. He sees a possible temporary moratorium lasting several months.

Privorotsky does not think the result means US data centres stop being built. He cites the market being up 19 for 19 over one-year forward periods after the last 19 midterm cycles, a possible acceleration in M&A in 2027, and says it is right to stay constructive on hyperscalers and higher quality tech.

Tony Kim (energy) says risk premium unwound on Monday and Tuesday on progress with Qatari mediators, with a peak-to-trough oil sell-off of about $20. In a full resolution oil could return to the low 80s, maybe mid 80s, where a floor forms as inventories are restocked. About 100 is fair and 115 prices in a large amount of risk premium.

Brad Shelofsky (IG credit) says the credit sell-off was orderly. He expects high quality hyperscalers to outperform neoclouds and AI equipment suppliers, since delayed capacity makes compute scarcer for hyperscalers while neoclouds with debt tied to delivery face delay risk. He says it has paid to sell rallies, and that the recent Microsoft, Oracle and Meta deals underwhelmed in size and duration.

GIR's Michael Ng says the US data centre buildout looks well supported through 2028. Under-construction capacity implies 22/24GW-IT of net adds in 2027/28 against GS forecasts of 20/24GW-IT, with another 137GW-gross of high-likelihood announced capacity as upside. The key risk is timing rather than cancellation, mainly in Texas, which is 20%/27% of 2027/28 under-construction additions.

GIR's Adam Bubes sees good visibility on US data centre construction growth through 2028, with a ~$900bn high-confidence pipeline and upgraded 2026-28 spend forecasts. He expects post-midterm restrictions to delay and extend the cycle into 2029/30 rather than reduce the total addressable market.

NZD rallied sharply after the National Party-led bloc (with ACT and NZ First) secured about 67 of 131 seats, reducing the risk of a shift back to the RBNZ's dual mandate with an employment objective. The official result is expected 27 Nov. GS Trading sees the move as mostly short covering after the RBNZ's surprise hold and weak labour data.
GS Trading prefers a long NZD bias on strong November seasonality but is reluctant to chase extremes given weak economic trends, and expects to eventually fade NZD strength.

GS FX strategy (Cahill) says slower AI construction or a lower chance of Middle East re-escalation would be negative for the Dollar over time, but is sceptical that sentiment has shifted as much as it appears. It sees the Dollar as still sensitive to AI-related risks through US relative returns that depend on tech.

GS FX suggests EUR downside options to hedge renewed energy price pressure, and says the Yen is best positioned to benefit from a sharp repricing of capex expectations. It is cautious on MXN because of asymmetric dovish policy risks.

Week ahead: US CPI Tuesday with GS core MoM +0.16% against consensus +0.2%, and US PPI Friday with GS final demand +0.3% against consensus +0.4%. China trade data Tuesday, BOJ minutes Tuesday, UK GDP and Brazil inflation Thursday, and US-mediated Russia/Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi through Nov 11.

tension_points.bull_case: GIR says under-construction capacity covers 2027/28 net adds, with a ~$900bn high-confidence pipeline, and restrictions are more likely to delay than cut the total market. Privorotsky says it is right to stay constructive on hyperscalers.
tension_points.bear_case: Phillips says state moratoria could affect up to about 40% of planned capacity in theory, and Privorotsky notes that throttling the build removes the main engine of EPS growth, making it hard to justify being long the rest of the market.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A temporary moratorium in Texas lasting more than several months, as Phillips expects, would push capacity to the right and raise costs.

tension_points.bull_case: Kim says full resolution could take oil back to the low 80s, maybe mid 80s, with a floor as inventories are restocked.
tension_points.bear_case: Kim says there is still a threat of escalation, and 115 is where a large amount of risk premium is priced in. GS FX also says energy moves may under-appreciate the uncertainties ahead.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Oil moving toward 115 would signal escalation risk premium returning.
